messages:
alex: Quick bench run — adaptive kernel sweep A100 vs H100 for llama-7B and llama-13B q8x4 in us-east and eu-west. TL;DR: H100 reduces p99 prefill by ~15–22% and boosts decode throughput ~25–35% on 13B, but $/1M tokens can still favor A100 in some steady-state configs because of instance pricing and batching efficiency.

alex: Test config: runtime main w/ --adaptive-kernel-selector, CUDA 12.1, cuBLAS tuned, same AMI, isolated nodes (no colocated tasks). Batches: prefill batch=1 (low-latency path), decode batch=8 for throughput runs. KV cache warm for decode tests.

alex: Raw table snapshot (median of 5 runs each, 95% CI):
```
Model | GPU  | prefill_p50_ms | prefill_p99_ms | decode_tokens_per_sec | tokens_per_1M_cost
7B q8x4 | A100 | 18             | 62             | 480k                  | $18.4
7B q8x4 | H100 | 14             | 50             | 640k                  | $22.2
13B q8x4| A100 | 35             | 110            | 260k                  | $26.8
13B q8x4| H100 | 28             | 86             | 336k                  | $31.5
```

sam: Nice. Two quick Qs: 1) which kernel paths were selected by the adaptive selector for prefill vs decode? 2) what batch sizes for decode/latency?

alex: 1) Prefill on H100 chose the tiled fused-attn + cuBLAS GEMM path most of the time; on A100 the selector sometimes fell back to the generic GEMM path when workspace fragmentation hit for long seqs. 2) Prefill tests were single-request cold/warm mix; decode throughput runs used batch=8, sequence length=512 average.

priya: Any region differences? eu-west vs us-east?

alex: eu-west adds ~8–12% p99 overhead vs us-east for prefill (measured across both GPUs) — likely network/storage latency + lower instance density (less ideal packing). Throughput scaling similar but cost per token moves slightly up in eu-west due to regional instance pricing.

maria: Did you try q4_0 / q4_1 or int8 variants? any quality regressions flagged?

alex: Only q8x4 for this sweep. Quick qualitative check on 50 eval prompts: q8x4 quality OK for 7B; 13B mild tokenization artifacts for rare tokens — will run eval harness next with rouge/embedding sim to catch regressions.

benchbot: Summary posted to dashboard: https://internal.redwood/perf/d/bench/2519876543 (contains full traces, p50/p95/p99 histograms, kernel breakdown). :rocket:

kevin: From an ops perspective, if H100 gives better p99 but costs more, what would you recommend for a PLG tier vs enterprise reserved pool?

alex: For PLG/shared hosted: favor A100 for 13B q8x4 to optimize $/1M tokens at steady-state (unless customer needs p99 guarantees). For enterprise/dedicated with SLA: H100 preferred when p99 and tail latency matter, or when smaller headroom for scaling is required. Also consider mixing: route latency-sensitive traffic to H100 and batch-heavy background work to A100.

sam: Any notes on kernel fallthrough events frequency? we should avoid pathological fallbacks during rollouts.

alex: Logged counts: fallback events ~0.7% of requests on A100 on longer prefill seqs, <0.1% on H100. Root cause = allocator fragmentation + tiled-attn workspace mismatch. Mitigation: tune allocator, bump workspace limit for tiled kernels, and make selector prefer tiled earlier for seq_len>256.

priya: Next steps?

alex: 1) run 24h steady-state jobs with traffic mix to validate $/1M tokens numbers; 2) run q4_0 / q4_1 + int8 sweep and full eval harness for quality regression; 3) create canary routing policy doc for hybrid deployment (H100 latency routes + A100 bulk). I'll open follow-up threads with the experiment IDs.

maria: Please tag me on the eval runs, I'll coordinate SLA test plan.

kevin: Sounds good, add cost-model snapshots to the canary doc so sales/finance can eyeball. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
